label: Factor radius
title: Under an idempotent observation the factor of a closed rule has radius at most 2 on the image, and the sixteen rule-200 cases are explained by that
kind: Exact audit of factor locality under five non-linear observations, with a theorem half and a census half
summary: Under the idempotent observations 200 and 4 the factor of every closed rule is the observation composed with the rule on the image, so its radius is at most 2; the sixteen rule-200 residual rules sit at exactly 2 and everything else at most 1. Under the non-idempotent observations 232, 32 and 22 every ring-independent closed rule has radius at most 1. The one exception is rule 223 at ring 6 under 22, closed at that ring only, whose factor needs a window covering the whole six-cell configuration.
takeaway: In this census the only closure that appears at one ring alone is also the only factor that needs the whole configuration in its window. That makes whole-ring support a useful warning sign here, not a proved characterization of finite-ring closures.
